Article:

Title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies, lower versus US dollar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher against most major currencies but lower against the US dollar on Wednesday, as the greenback strengthened broadly amid renewed concerns over Europe's fiscal outlook, an analyst said.
At 6 pm, the ringgit eased to 4.0850/0895 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0835/0880.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.42 per cent to 102.26 points, as major currencies such as the euro, which carries the largest weighting in the DXY, depreciated 0.69 per cent against the US dollar to 1.1181.
"Still, concerns over Europe's fiscal trajectory have led to a stronger US dollar.
"Thus far, the ringgit has maintained a tight range against the US dollar, with the ringgit-dollar pair hovering between RM4.0840 and RM4.0885 today," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
The local note gained against the Japanese yen to 2.5797/5827 from 2.5807/5837 at Tuesday's close, appreciated against the British pound to 5.4049/4108 from 5.4066/4125, and strengthened against the euro to 4.5740/5790 from 4.5907/5957 previously.
Meanwhile, the ringgit was mixed against its ASEAN peers.
It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1919/1957 from 3.1935/1975 at Tuesday's close and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.1217/1386 from 12.1424/1609 previously.
However, it depreciated against the Philippine peso to 6.51/6.52 from 6.50/6.51 at Tuesday's close, and was marginally lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 228.3/228.7 versus 228.1/228.4 previously

Title: Focus on 'civilisational harmony' over division, Anwar says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's rich diversity, shaped over millennia by different cultures and religions, must be protected against the rise of divisive identity politics, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said toxic identity politics and populism driven by anti-immigration, ethnic hatred, and xenophobia are gaining traction globally and threatening democratic processes.
He added that Malaysia is not immune, with certain quarters stoking racial and religious tensions in a desperate bid for political power.
​"I earnestly believe that all right-minded people should shun such reckless and vile attempts.
"Politics aside, it behoves us not to allow differences to fester into permanent sources of division," he said at the Islam-Confucian Civilisational Cultural Festival.
His speech was delivered by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir.
Anwar said identity should never be used as a tool to fracture society.
"Instead, Malaysia's engagement with global partners like China reflects a broader commitment to multicultural harmony and civilisational exchange," he said.
​
He added that the world today does not need more walls but more bridges.
"It does not require us to abandon our identities in order to live together.
"It requires us to have the confidence to understand our own traditions, while remaining open to the wisdom of others.
"We should honour this tradition of civilisational exchange, and renew this spirit of learning and mutual respect as we respond to the challenges of our time."
​Anwar said he hoped the spirit of mutual respect and learning will guide the summit and help address contemporary global challenges.

Title: AMEC seeks essential status for courier sector
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Association of Malaysian Express Carriers (AMEC) has urged the government to recognise the courier industry as essential infrastructure supporting the national digital economy and resilience in the 2027 Budget.
AMEC president Ronald Tan said the budget provided an opportunity to strengthen conditions allowing courier companies to invest, improve productivity and serve businesses and consumers over the long term.
"Malaysia's digital economy depends on dependable delivery networks," he said.
Tan said the 2027 Budget should support industry modernisation through technology adoption, operational efficiency and workforce development.
This will enable courier companies to improve service quality and meet changing customer expectations.
AMEC said a commercially sustainable operating environment was important to enable courier companies to invest in their networks, develop their workforce and maintain reliable services nationwide.
It said continued improvements in productivity, service quality and innovation would support the industry's long-term sustainability.
The association also highlighted the importance of nationwide connectivity, including in Sabah, Sarawak and rural communities, alongside a skilled workforce and safe working practices.
AMEC said the courier industry contributed to national resilience by supporting supply-chain continuity and the movement of essential goods, including during disruptions and emergencies.
It said investment in infrastructure modernisation, operational preparedness and protection against physical and cyber risks would further strengthen the industry's resilience.
AMEC welcomed continued engagement with the government and relevant stakeholders on practical measures to strengthen the industry.
It hoped the 2027 Budget initiatives would be accompanied by effective implementation and clear follow-through to deliver tangible benefits to businesses, workers and consumers.
"A healthy courier industry supports business growth and the communities it serves.," Tan said.

Title: Lawyer says estate administrators did not enrich themselves
Article:
Pix Shahril Badri
KUALA LUMPUR: The administrators of late Genting heiress Lim Siew Kim's RM1.6 billion estate did not enrich themselves through legal fees paid from the estate, the High Court heard.
Lawyer B. Thangaraj, representing interim administrators pendente lite (APLs) Datuk S. Satharuban and Khoo Siew Kiat, said the payments were expenses incurred while carrying out their duties to preserve and protect the estate.
He said the APLs' appointment order empowered them to preserve, protect and manage the deceased's assets and pay lawful debts of the estate.
He said Siew Kim's will stated that testamentary expenses, including legal fees, were to be paid from the estate.
"These are fees payable in respect of them acting for the executors and in estate matters.
"In these circumstances, the fees are to be borne by the estate.
"So these are definitely lawful debts of the estate," he submitted.
Thangaraj said there was transparency and no evidence of misconduct in defending the will.
He said the APLs were not beneficiaries of the estate and were merely carrying out their responsibilities in administering and protecting its assets.
On Monday, the court was told that the interim administrators had allegedly paid lawyers over RM2 million without approval, breaching a court order.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1548308/genting-founders-grandson-seeks-removal-late-mothers-rm16b-estate
Thangaraj dismissed allegations that the APLs had acted outside the scope of their court order.
He said the APLs had taken steps to protect the estate, including seeking financial documents and preventing fixed deposits from being uplifted.
He said parties dissatisfied with the APLs' actions could apply to the court for further directions instead of seeking their removal.
Judge Datuk Mahazan Mat Taib fixed Nov 13 to deliver her decision.
Satharuban and Khoo were appointed by the High Court on Nov 27, 2023, to manage the estate as APLs amid an ongoing family dispute over the validity of Siew Kim's will.
Siew Kim, the third child of late Genting Group of Companies founder Tan Sri Lim Goh Tong, died of cancer in July 2022 at the age of 73.
She left three daughters and an only son, Marcus Chan Jau Chwen, 42, who is seeking the removal of the administrators.
Siew Kim's daughters, Chan T'shiao Li and Kimberly Chan Tshiao Miin, are challenging the validity of a will said to have been executed on April 28, 2022, arguing that their mother lacked testamentary capacity due to her medical condition before her death.
The first and second defendants in the sisters' suit are Malcolm Fernandez and Chan Mei Yee, the executors and trustees named in the April 28, 2022 will.
The third and fourth defendants are Marcus and lawyer Datuk Low Beng Choo, who drafted, prepared and executed the will.

Title: Indonesia's ex-anti-graft prosecutor on trial after US$19m, 70kg gold seized
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's former top anti-graft prosecutor went on trial on money laundering charges on Wednesday, months after he was arrested with millions of dollars in cash and 70kg of gold bars found at his home and other properties.
Southeast Asia's biggest economy has long struggled with corruption and has arrested scores of public officials in recent years.
Febrie Adriansyah is accused of wrongdoing with public money while serving as Indonesia's top anti-corruption prosecutor. He denies the accusations.
He stepped down in July after more than four years in the role following the raids on the properties, including his house outside Jakarta.
Investigators seized US$19 million in various currencies and 74kg of gold bars worth millions more.
"He has participated in committing a criminal act... as a civil servant or state official, with the intent of unlawfully benefiting himself or another person, or by abusing his power to coerce someone," the indictment read.
The Attorney General's Office accuses Febrie of extortion and money laundering in a case involving state insurance companies.
Febrie filed a request to the court in August for police to return the money and gold seized from his properties.
Indonesia scored a low 34 out of 100 on watchdog Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index for 2025.--AFP

Title: Wisma Putra to restructure to address overseas staffing shortages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Foreign Ministry is working with several agencies to develop a restructuring plan to address staffing shortages affecting its operations, including at diplomatic missions overseas.
Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said the ministry was working closely with the Public Service Department and the Finance Ministry on the restructuring exercise to strengthen service delivery and resolve human resource issues.
He said staffing shortages at the ministry were partly due to the temporary freeze on recruitment for several public service schemes, a challenge also faced by other ministries and agencies.
"The vacancies are caused by various factors, including the absence of recruitment for several schemes in the public service, which were temporarily frozen.
"The issue of manpower shortages is also faced by all ministries and agencies, including the Foreign Ministry," he said when winding up the debate on the Auditor General's Report in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Lukanisman said the ministry took seriously the audit findings on unfilled positions at several Malaysian diplomatic missions, particularly in Jakarta and Beijing.
He said the deployment of officers to Malaysian diplomatic missions abroad had to take into account the ministry's existing financial and human resources, while postings were planned according to service requirements, the priorities of bilateral relations and the direction of the country's foreign policy.
"To face this challenge, the Foreign Ministry needs to continue optimising its existing workforce to ensure all diplomatic and administrative functions can be carried out effectively," he said.
Lukanisman said the filling of overseas posts was also subject to the control and approval of central agencies, including PSD and the Finance Ministry, to ensure it remained aligned with public service policies and the government's financial capacity.
The Auditor General's Report 2/2026, tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on Monday, found that four home-based staff positions at the Malaysian embassy in Jakarta and two at the embassy in Beijing remained vacant despite being provided for under approved staffing warrants.
Six locally recruited positions at the Beijing embassy were also reported vacant between 2017 and 2025.
Lukanisman said the ministry was also taking steps to optimise existing manpower while working with central agencies on the restructuring plan.
He said the exercise was aimed at further strengthening the ministry's service delivery while addressing the human resource challenges it faced.

Title: Indonesia jails 35 Indian nationals over Bali online gambling ring
Article:
DENPASAR: An Indonesian court sentenced dozens of Indian nationals to prison on Wednesday for their involvement in an online gambling operation on the resort island of Bali.
Gambling is illegal in the Muslim-majority archipelago, with punishments extended to bookmakers, punters, those who promote gambling content online and gamblers themselves.
Police arrested 39 Indian nationals in February at two villas in separate locations on Bali and charged 35 of them.
The group entered Indonesia on tourist visas and had been promoting and managing transactions for an online gambling site since late last year, according to the police.
Presiding judge Putu Gde Novyartha found the men guilty in a Wednesday hearing, sentencing most of them to two years behind bars. Two were sentenced to two and a half years.
The judge also ordered "the defendants to be deported after serving the sentence... and once the sentence has been completed, the defendants are prohibited from visiting the territory of the Republic of Indonesia."
The operation brought in up to eight billion rupiah (about US$450,000) a month, police said.
Turnover linked to online gambling in Indonesia reached more than 280 trillion rupiah last year, official data showed, with more than 12 million of the country's 287 million citizens estimated to be engaged in the illicit activity, most of them as gamblers.
Authorities said in May they would review the visa-free entry policy for nationals of Southeast Asian countries after a string of arrests of foreigners accused of running illegal gambling and scam operations.
Investigators have found that many of those allegedly involved in an illegal gambling centre in Jakarta had entered Indonesia using visa waivers or applied for permits on arrival.--AFP

Title: Wan Fayhsal rushed to HKL, in stable condition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Machang member of parliament Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal was rushed to Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) for emergency treatment today.
His private secretary, Wan Meor Safwat Naqiuddin Shamsudin, said Wan Fayhsal had been admitted and was in stable condition.
He said doctors advised the lawmaker to rest until he had fully recovered.

The statement did not disclose the reason for Wan Fayhsal's emergency treatment.

Title: Khaled: LCS still operable without NSM as it has other weapons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) will still be able to operate despite not having a surface-to-surface missile as it has other weapons and combat systems.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the absence of the Naval Strike Missile (NSM) did not mean the LCS would be received without any weapons systems.
"I would like to correct the understanding slightly. Although the LCS does not have the NSM, it is not the case that the LCS we receive later will be completely without any weapons systems," he said when winding up the debate on the Auditor-General's Report 2/2026 in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said the LCS would still be equipped with several other weapons systems, including surface-to-air missiles and anti-submarine warfare systems.

Title: Govt seeks solution for damaged RM23.7mil Sabah housing project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is assessing solutions to address structural problems at a RM23.7 million People's Housing Programme (PPR) project in Beaufort, Sabah.
Its minister, Nga Kor Ming, said the project, completed in 2017, remained unoccupied due to structural damage caused by ground movement.
"Our investigations, through the Public Works Department, found serious structural cracks in one terrace block comprising eight housing units.
"Five units in another block are experiencing moderate cracking caused by soil settlement, affecting the stability and structural integrity of the entire building," he said when winding up the debate on the Auditor-General's Report 2/2026 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Although the eight affected units had been demolished, Nga said continued ground movement prevented the repair works from being completed.
He said the ministry also conducted forensic testing and geotechnical investigations between October 2024 and May 2025.
He said the geotechnical analysis found that the primary cause of the structural failure was an uneven soil strata profile at the construction site.
He said the situation was exacerbated by the presence of soft soil layers and high organic content, which directly caused ground instability due to uneven settlement.
Nga said the findings were also supported by structural integrity tests conducted in two phases from August 2025 to May this year.
"Overall, laboratory analysis from both phases confirmed that the actual compressive strength of the concrete was inconsistent and failed to meet the design strength requirements," he said.
All 67 units under the RM23.7 million PPR project in Kampung Selagon, Beaufort, which was completed in 2017, remained unoccupied as of July 2026 due to structural damage caused by ground movement.

Title: Malaysia weighs missile options from South Korea, France, Turkiye for LCS
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is considering missile systems from South Korea, France and Turkiye as alternatives to the Naval Strike Missile (NSM) for its Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said South Korea's LIG, Turkiye's Roketsan and France's MBDA were among the suppliers being considered.
"We are weighing all this and we will ensure that the delivery and installation period is not longer, or excessively long, like the Norwegian contract, which took up to eight years," he said when winding up the debate on the Auditor-General's Report 2/2026 in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said missile purchases Malaysia had made, was making or planned to make from LIG, Roketsan and MBDA had delivery periods of around three years.

Title: Nobel Peace Prize haunted by the 'spectre' of Trump
Article:
DONALD Trump's chances of winning the Nobel Peace Prize are seen as minimal, but his "spectre" will cast its shadow over Friday's announcement of the winner in Oslo, experts say.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee knows it will be under close scrutiny: since his return to the White House in January 2025, the billionaire Republican has campaigned intensively for the prize and hasn't hidden his disappointment at not winning it yet.
The chances of him getting the nod are however undermined by his war against Iran, his territorial ambitions – sometimes at the expense of allies, as in Greenland – and his attacks on international cooperation institutions and the media.
Even though he has not been lobbying as openly for the Nobel in recent weeks, Trump remains on everyone's minds, with strong chances that the committee's pick will, regardless of who they choose, be interpreted as direct or indirect criticism of the US president.
Trump is "the spectre in the room", said the head of the Peace Research Institute in Oslo (PRIO), Haakon Gjerlow.
He said the Nobel committee must be asking itself: "Is there any potential for this prize to create harm rather than good in awarding it?", given the reactions that could emerge from the White House.
The Nobel Institute says it is unfazed.
"There's always a lot of lobbying, and ultimately perhaps also attempts to exert pressure on the committee. So in one sense we're very used to that,"  the secretary of the committee, Kristian Berg Harpviken, told AFP.
"It's not something we don't discuss. Of course we have to discuss it, but it's not like that influences the discussions in the room and decisions that come out," he insisted.
Last year, the prestigious prize went to Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, a choice generally considered palatable to Trump.
Machado even gave him her Nobel gold medal, judging he deserved it after the capture of President Nicolas Maduro – though she failed to obtain his political backing in exchange.
[[nid:1549862]]
Those events could prompt the committee to this year choose a laureate who enjoys broad consensus, such as an individual or organisation working to protect children or humanitarian efforts.
That could include the Save the Children charity and Mykola Kuleba, a Ukrainian children's rights activist campaigning for the return of kids illegally taken to Russia from occupied territories – a cause close to the heart of Trump's wife Melania.
Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms (ERR), a vast network of volunteers risking their lives to help people facing the double threat of war and hunger, could also be a potential laureate.
But the committee may also choose a laureate that could rub Trump the wrong way.
That could include the UN special rapporteur for the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese, Pope Leo XIV, press freedoms with an award to the Committee to Protect Journalists, or international justice bodies such as the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the International Court of Justice (ICJ).
"We live in an age of predators. We have Trump, Putin, Netanyahu," said Nobel historian Asle Sveen.
"They don't want to have an international order. They want to have big powers with spheres of influence. And this court stands in the way," he said, referring to the ICC.
A total of 287 individuals and organisations have been nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize, though the names on the list are kept secret for 50 years.
But peace remains elusive in many parts of the world: 65 armed conflicts involving at least one state actor were registered in 2025, the highest number since 1946, according to PRIO.
"At an overall level, it is clear that the world is not developing in the right direction," said Harpviken.
"At the same time ... there is no lack of good initiatives. There is no lack of organisations or individuals who do good work," he said.
"A peace prize may make more sense than ever."
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Northern Solar secures RM34mil EPCC project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Northern Solar Holdings Bhd, through its wholly owned subsidiary Northern Solar Sdn Bhd, has secured a RM34 million engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) contract for the development of a 9.50-megawatt (MW) large-scale solar photovoltaic plant.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said the letter of award (LOA) for the project was accepted on Oct 7, 2026.
It said the project is scheduled to achieve commercial operation by May 1, 2027.
"Due to the confidential provision in the LOA, the identity of the party who awarded the LOA is not disclosed," it said.
The company said the project is expected to contribute positively to the group's earnings and net assets per share for the financial years ending March 31, 2027 onwards.
"The board said it does not foresee any exceptional risks arising from the project other than normal operational and execution risks," it added.

Title: LCS 1 delivery delayed again, now targeted for April 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The delivery of the first Littoral Combat Ship (LCS 1) has been delayed to April 2027, four months later than the latest December 2026 target.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said contractor Lumut Naval Shipyard Sdn Bhd (Lunas) had informed the ministry that it could no longer meet its earlier commitment to deliver LCS 1 in December.
He said the delay was due to outstanding works, including piping, cabling, equipment installation and inspection, followed by testing and commissioning.
"Lunas has informed me that it cannot fulfil its previous commitment and guarantee that LCS 1 can be delivered in December 2026.
"Instead, Lunas has given a new date, with LCS 1 expected to be delivered in April 2027," he said when winding up the debate on the Auditor-General's Report in the Dewan Rakyat.

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends lower as higher US yields, oil prices weigh on sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended lower today in tandem with weaker regional markets, failing to track Wall Street's rally as elevated US Treasury yields and renewed gains in crude oil weighed on sentiment.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 21.57 points to 1,611.78 from Tuesday's close of 1,633.35.
The benchmark index opened 0.19 of a point higher at 1,633.54, marking its intraday high, and hit a low of 1,610.55 in the late afternoon session.
On the broader market, losers surpassed gainers 663 to 492, while 508 counters were unchanged, 1,127 untraded and 13 suspended.
Turnover decreased to 3.83 billion units worth RM3.52 billion, compared with 4.18 billion units worth RM2.95 billion yesterday.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Brent crude oil rose above US$101 per barrel following Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, rekindling concerns over West Asia supply disruptions.
"Meanwhile, the US 10-year Treasury yield remained near 5.3 per cent, while the 30-year yield stayed above 5.6 per cent, keeping investors cautious over the outlook for inflation and monetary easing," he told Bernama.
Back home, Thong said market sentiment is likely to remain cautious after the benchmark index broke below the 1,625-1,630 support levels, suggesting that near-term selling pressure has yet to fully subside.
"For the rest of the week, attention will turn to Budget 2027 on Friday, which could provide fresh domestic catalysts. However, elevated crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions in West Asia and high global bond yields are likely to keep investors defensive," he added.
Among the heavyweights, Maybank slipped 10 sen to RM9.87, Public Bank slid eight sen to RM4.59, CIMB gave up 37 sen to RM7.33, Tenaga Nasional shed four sen to RM12.86, and IHH Healthcare eased one sen to RM7.90.
In active trade, Top Glove fell two sen to 85.5 sen, Zetrix AI declined one sen to eight sen, V.S Industry edged down half a sen to 32.5 sen, and Supermax Corporation erased 1.5 sen to 44.5 sen, while Metronic Global was flat at half a sen.
Among the top gainers, Mi Technovation jumped 38 sen to RM6.38, Batu Kawan climbed 32 sen to RM19.60, Malaysian Pacific Industries increased 24 sen to RM45.20, Petronas Dagangan rose 20 sen to RM19.32, and Gas Malaysia improved 16 sen to RM5.25.
Top losers were led by Nestle, which declined RM2.24 to RM89.02, Fraser & Neave lost 94 sen to RM20.78, Hong Leong Bank trimmed 58 sen to RM21.50, while Hong Leong Financial Group and Allianz Malaysia shaved off 44 sen each to RM17.90 and RM20.18, respectively.

Title: RM1mil fund launched for intellectual property valuation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has allocated RM1 million for a fund to cover the cost of professional intellectual property valuation services.
Its minister, Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali, said the fund was for eligible local companies to have their intellectual property assets systematically and professionally valued.
"Their intangible assets involving intellectual property can therefore be officially valued to support banking financing, licensing and investment.
"This is particularly important for start-ups and technology-based small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with valuable intellectual property assets.
"Many face difficulties obtaining bank financing because they do not have traditional physical collateral," he said in a statement in conjunction with the 2026 National Intellectual Property Commercialisation Conference and Exhibition.
Armizan said another initiative was the introduction of Malaysia's first Intellectual Property Valuation Module, which would serve as a basis for developing more uniform valuation standards.
He said it was also expected to support efforts to train qualified local intellectual property valuation experts through a structured and regulated system.
"Both initiatives complement each other in developing a more structured intellectual property-backed financing ecosystem.
"The financing fund will help companies obtain valuation services, while the module will strengthen capacity, expertise and standards in carrying out the valuation process," he said.

Title: Hamzah ex aide's trial: Witness insists office existed for alleged money handover
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A prosecution witness in the corruption trial of a former political secretary to former Home Minister Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today maintained that the Yayasan Tanah Aku office in Publika, where RM350,000 in alleged commission payments were handed over, did exist.
Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NSB) managing director Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, said this during cross-examination by counsel Datuk Yaacob Md Sam, who is representing Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad.
Yaacob: I put it to you that the handover of RM100,000 on Dec 4, 2020 and RM250,000 on Dec 16, 2020 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir did not take place, because the said office did not exist.
Wan Azhar: I disagree.
In his witness statement, Wan Azhar stated that Sayed Amir asked him to pay RM350,000 in cash as part of a five per cent commission, after assisting NSB secure a police project tender.
"I handed over RM100,000 in a paper bag to Sayed around 4 pm on Dec 4, 2020, and RM250,000, also in a paper bag, at 3.30 pm on Dec 16, 2020. On both occasions, only Sayed and I were present," he said in his witness statement.
The 17th prosecution witness said he had accompanied a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer to Publika to identify the said location, and found the unit in question to be closed, with no signage indicating that it was the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku.
Wan Azhar, however, disagreed with Yaacob's suggestion that both units were vacant and unoccupied on the said dates.
Yaacob: The owner of the premises gave evidence that, prior to the signing of the tenancy agreement, both units had been occupied by a law firm. That firm vacated the premises at the end of 2019. We therefore put it to you that from the end of 2019 until Jan 1, 2021, no office occupied either unit. Do you agree?
Wan Azhar: I went to the location only twice, on Dec 4 and 16, 2020. I therefore know only that it was in operation on those two dates. On other days, I cannot be certain whether it was in operation or vacant.
On May 23, 2024, Sayed Amir 44, was charged on two counts of receiving RM350,000 in gratification from Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof as inducement for assisting NSB secure the RMPNet tender for the police valued at RM381,112,042.44.
The offences allegedly occurred at the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku, Solaris Dutamas, here, at 4 pm on Dec 4, 2020 and at 3.30 pm on Dec 16, 2020, respectively.
Sayed Amir was also charged with soliciting RM350,000 in gratification from the same individual, for a similar purpose, at the Shah Alam office of NSB in early December 2020.
The charges were brought under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years' imprisonment and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The trial before Judge Rosli Ahmad resumes tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget must make every ringgit count: Accountants group
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia enters 2027 Budget from a stronger fiscal position, but the next phase of consolidation will require greater focus on how revenue is raised and public funds are spent.
Malaysia Management Accountants Association president Dr Abdul Ahad Mohd Salleh said the fiscal deficit had narrowed from 6.4 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2021 to 3.7 per cent in 2025.
But the government must maintain discipline while households grapple with cost pressures and businesses face an uncertain global environment.
"Raising more revenue is not necessarily successful if the method creates disproportionate costs elsewhere in the economy.
"Equally, a larger allocation does not by itself show that a programme has worked," he said.
Abdul Ahad said the 2027 Budget should give greater weight to outcome-based spending, with major programmes clearly linking allocations to the problem being addressed, expected outcomes, timelines and the agencies responsible.
For example, healthcare spending should be assessed not only by the amount allocated but also by improvements in access and waiting times, while business facilitation could be measured through approval times and reductions in administrative burdens.
"The allocation tells us what the government intends to spend; the outcome tells us whether it worked," he said.
On tax reform, Abdul Ahad said if the Sales and Service Tax (SST) remains, the government should examine areas where tax cascading was creating avoidable costs for businesses.
Targeted credits, offsets or business-to-business relief could be considered where they deliver clear benefits without creating excessive documentation, verification or refund requirements.
He also called for deeper study of a possible SST-GST hybrid model, including the implications for different sectors.
One option could be retaining SST for services while considering GST for manufacturing, where businesses could potentially recover input tax, reducing costs that could eventually benefit consumers through lower selling prices.
On e-Invoicing, Abdul Ahad said the system should deliver benefits beyond enforcement.
With businesses below RM3 million in annual sales or income exempted, the government should use the structured data generated by e-Invoicing to reduce duplicate reporting, speed up legitimate verification and make enforcement more risk-based.
"Digitalisation should ultimately mean better information for the government and less unnecessary administration for compliant businesses," he said.
Abdul Ahad said competitiveness should also be measured beyond tax incentives, with businesses placing importance on policy predictability, approval times, compliance costs and ease of operating after an investment is made.
The 2027 Budget could therefore strengthen competitiveness through clearer implementation timelines, fewer overlaps between agencies and greater certainty over major policy changes, alongside targeted incentives.
Household assistance should likewise become more targeted, he said, as income alone does not fully capture financial pressure.
Households with similar incomes can face very different costs depending on housing, dependants, childcare, healthcare and caring responsibilities.
"Better data should allow assistance to be targeted according to where pressure is concentrated and which intervention is most appropriate, rather than defaulting to broad-based support," he said.
Abdul Ahad also called for greater medium-term visibility on tax reforms, spending priorities and implementation timelines over the next three to five years.
While Malaysia already has medium-term fiscal planning, clearer forward guidance would give businesses and households greater certainty, he said.
"The 2027 Budget will first be judged by what is announced. The more important test is what those measures achieve," Abdul Ahad said.
"Malaysia has made progress in restoring fiscal discipline.
"The next stage should be about making the fiscal system work better - connecting spending to outcomes, reducing tax and administrative friction, targeting support more precisely and giving businesses and households greater certainty about what comes next."

Title: Mayor of opposition stronghold Izmir defects to Erdogan party
Article:
ANKARA: The mayor of Izmir, Turkiye's third city and an opposition stronghold, on Wednesday defected to the ruling AKP, in a huge symbolic victory for Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
Mayor Cemil Tugay's decision to join the Islamic-rooted Justice and Development Party (AKP) was announced by Erdogan at a parliamentary group meeting in Ankara where he welcomed the mayor in a party-like atmosphere broadcast live on TV.
"I welcome Izmir Mayor Cemil Tugay who is today joining the AKP family," Erdogan said as Tugay walked onto the stage and was handed a party pin.
Taking control of the mayorship of Izmir, a secular stronghold on Turkey's Aegean coast which has long been governed by opposition social democrats, is a major coup for Erdogan.
But although it helps AKP expand its influence in Izmir, it does not mean the party has a majority on the city's metropolitan municipal council, which remains dominated by the opposition.
The defection comes as Turkiye's opposition battles an increasingly intense crackdown, with a barrage of what observers say are politically motivated arrests and lawsuits targeting its mayors and elected officials.
The crackdown followed the main opposition CHP's resounding victory in the March 2024 local elections, trouncing AKP in a major blow for Erdogan.
Since then, CHP has faced growing intimidation campaign that has seen six of its provincial mayors arrested, including Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, and 29 of its district mayors, 13 in Istanbul, according to figures published Wednesday by the independent Diken news website.
Alongside the lawsuits, there has been a growing number of defections to AKP, with at least 17 opposition mayors switching to AKP, Medyascope news website said last week ahead of Tugay's defection.
Tugay's decision came after weeks of rumours that he was planning to switch.
"We love Izmir. May it benefit everyone," Tugay told reporters as he walked into the AKP headquarters where a huge crowd inside the auditorium was raucously chanting, clapping and cheering as Erdogan started to speak
"Izmir is proud of you!" they shouted.
Tugay was elected Izmir mayor in April 2024 just after CHP's local election victory.
But in June this year, he resigned from the party after a controversial court ruling plunged CHP into crisis, ousting its leader Ozgur Ozel who left to form the Yeni (New) Party – which is now Turkiye's main opposition
Despite leaving, Tugay did not follow Ozel, saying he would remain independent, with rumours emerging over the summer that he was considering defecting to AKP – all of which he denied.
Speculation intensified last week after Tugay met Erdogan at the presidential palace in Ankara.
Addressing a Yeni party meeting in parliament on Tuesday, Ozel spoke of the campaign of pressure, threats and blackmail faced by Izmir's elected officials.
"Those who do not bow to this pressure... will remain our brothers until the day they die. But those who sell out and leave are traitors," he said.
According to figures on the municipality's website, Yeni is the largest group in the 184-member council with 91 seats, followed by the AKP with 38 and the CHP with 35.
If Tugay joins the AKP, its representation would rise to 39 seats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yinson prices US$1.46bil Agogo FPSO bonds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Production, through its subsidiary Yinson Azalea Production Pte Ltd, has priced US$1.46 billion in bonds to refinance its Agogo floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel.
The bonds, which are fully amortising with a scheduled maturity of 13.3 years, were priced at 98.164 per cent of their principal amount.
They carry a fixed annual coupon of 6.517 per cent, payable semi-annually.
Yinson said the proceeds will refinance existing debt related to the Agogo FPSO, fund required reserve accounts, pay transaction-related fees and expenses and allow for equity distributions from excess proceeds.
The Agogo FPSO is leased to Azule Energy Angola S.p.A. under a 15-year firm bareboat charter, with extension options of up to five years, and operates in Block 15/06 offshore Angola.
The notes are expected to settle on Oct 21, 2026, with an application made for them to be admitted to trading on the London Stock Exchange's International Securities Market under the Bloomberg ticker YPAGAO.
Fitch and Moody's have assigned expected credit ratings of BBB+ and Baa2 respectively.
This reflects the Agogo FPSO's credit fundamentals, its strategic importance to the charterer and the role of FPSOs in the offshore oil and gas value chain.
Yinson Production chief financial officer Markus Wenker said the group is pleased with the strong support from institutional investors for this offering.
This is the company's third FPSO project bond in three years and sets a new benchmark as the largest FPSO project bond to date.
"It also represents an important milestone for the asset class as a whole, as this is the
first FPSO project bond outside Brazil, broadening and diversifying the investable universe for investors seeking exposure to infrastructure assets backed by highly visible cash flows and strong counterparties," he said in a statement.
He added that the transaction demonstrates the availability of long-term capital to the FPSO industry, reinforces the merits of the lease-and-operate model and further strengthens Yinson Production's capital structure.

Title: RM8.08bil govt loan arrears manageable, says Finance Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The RM8.084 billion in outstanding federal government loans is manageable and has declined from an average of 21 per cent between 2020 and 2022.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the outstanding amount as at Dec 31 last year represented 15.67 per cent of total repayments due.
"The amount is manageable and has been declining compared with the average of 21 per cent recorded between 2020 and 2022," he said.
Previously, the Auditor General's Report Series 2/2026 found that the Finance Ministry collected only RM465 million, or five per cent, of the RM9.273 billion in loan arrears carried over from 2024.
As of Dec 31, outstanding loan arrears stood at RM8.084 billion, with RM5.024 billion, or 62.1 per cent, having remained unpaid for more than six years.
The report also found that new arrears totalling RM16.15 million emerged even after some loans had been restructured between one and five times, with repayment periods extended by between 10 and 40 years.
Liew said the RM8.084 billion comprised RM5.709 billion in outstanding principal and RM2.375 billion in outstanding interest and late-payment interest.
He said most of the arrears involved loans for basic public infrastructure projects, including clean water supply, sewerage, public housing, low-cost housing and public transport.
"The category of borrowers with the highest loan arrears is companies at 62 per cent, followed by state governments at around 32 per cent," he said when winding up for his ministry during the debate on the AG's Report.
Liew said the government was also looking to differentiate between projects with commercial potential and those undertaken primarily to fulfil social obligations.
"The Finance Ministry recommends that any project that constitutes a social obligation be funded through development expenditure in the form of grants rather than commercial loans," he said.
He said the approach would reduce the financial burden on borrowers undertaking projects intended primarily to provide public services.
He added that the government was also proposing a mandatory collateral requirement for new loans involving state governments and companies under the Minister of Finance Incorporated.
"For new loan applications involving state governments or Minister of Finance Incorporated companies, the government will require collateral, such as land assets, equivalent to the value of the loan, to enable a claim to be made in the event of a repayment default," he said.

Title: Kosovo parliament elects new president, avoiding snap election
Article:
PRISTINA: Kosovo's parliament elected economist Justina Shiroka Pula as the country's largely ceremonial president just before a constitutional deadline, avoiding another snap election in one of the poorest countries in Europe.
She received 81 votes, one more than she needed, in the 120-seat parliament in the early minutes of Wednesday.
Failure to elect a new president would have triggered snap parliamentary elections in the Balkan country, as it did in June.
"This mandate does not belong to just one person. It belongs to our citizens... I will be the president of all citizens," Shiroka Pula said after the vote.
Shiroka Pula's election followed a deal between the ruling Vetevendosje party of Prime Minister Albin Kurti and opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo to limit the powers of a Kosovo war crimes court in The Hague.
Police fired tear gas and used water cannon on Monday to disperse demonstrators demanding the changes be approved.
Critics have asserted the Hague court's punishments are too harsh.
The court on Sept 16 sentenced former President Hashim Thaci and three others to a combined 81 years in prison for war crimes during the territory's violent break from Serbia in 1998-1999.
The presidency is mainly ceremonial in Kosovo but has often been a source of political instability because a two-thirds parliamentary majority is needed to elect a president and parties have struggled to agree on a candidate.
Shiroka Pula, born in 1953, is the president of Kosovo's Academy of Sciences and Arts and an economics professor who served as minister of the economy between 2008 and 2011.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MBPP disposes of more than 3,600 pest birds in September
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) disposed of 3,626 pest birds in September as part of its ongoing population control efforts.
The figure comprised 1,616 pigeons and 2,010 crows. A total of 105 crow nests were also destroyed during operations conducted in areas under MBPP's administration.
The city council said the measures were aimed at maintaining cleanliness, safeguarding public health and ensuring the well-being of the urban environment.
"We also took enforcement action against people who fed birds in public areas, issuing five compounds under Section 47(1)(g) of the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974.
"The control and enforcement measures will be carried out continuously to reduce the nuisance caused by pest birds and minimise pollution and cleanliness risks that could affect community comfort," it said on its Facebook page.
MBPP wants the public not to feed birds indiscriminately, particularly in public areas, as the practice could contribute to an increase in bird populations and create environmental cleanliness and health issues.
It said public cooperation was essential to ensure bird population management and control efforts could be carried out effectively to create a clean, safe and comfortable urban environment for all.

Title: 'It's personal': Fiji minister pushes better climate finance at pre-COP
Article:
NADI: Fiji's climate change minister wants streamlined access to financial assistance for Pacific nations, telling AFP on Wednesday the issue was "personal", with waves washing away parts of her own village.
Lynda Tabuya has partnered with Australian counterpart Chris Bowen to lead the "pre-COP" meeting in Nadi and Tuvalu, a precursor to the larger UN-sponsored global climate summit – known as COP31 – to be held in Turkiye next month.
She told AFP one of her main messages to delegates in Nadi was the need to speed up the distribution of money for climate solutions.
"It's frustrating at times," Tabuya said. "We even feel it on a government level.
"Even after we've secured finance, it takes a long process," she added.
"Some have even taken three to five years, where the access to climate finance is quite difficult."
Tabuya's own village of Tiliva on the island Kadavu, about 90 kilometres south of Fiji's main island, has been affected by rising seas.
"We've lost about four metres (13 feet) of the shoreline to sea level rise," Tabuya said.
"Some families have had to relocate to the hills, but even in high tide the ground is soggy because the water doesn't recede."
It took her village, which is off the energy grid, more than a decade to secure finance for a solar system.
She said climate finance is taking far too long, and loans are not a solution.
"Part of our appeal going to COP is to make the current finance structure to be restructured so that it's simplified," Tabuya said.
"It's frustrating. We are the least emitters in the Pacific, and yet we are the most disproportionately affected.
"So we appeal to the world to look more at grant-based finance because it will fund a seawall, like I need in my village. So it's very personal."
It's one reason Pacific Island nations are trying to take climate finance into their own hands.
Regional leaders have set up the Pacific Resilience Facility (PRF) with the hopes of raising US$500 million, but so far have brought in commitments for less than half of that.
Fiji announced on Wednesday an additional US$10 million for that fund, with the United Kingdom giving 10 million pounds (US$13.2 million).
The UK's climate envoy, Rachel Kyte, told AFP on the sidelines of the meetings that the PRF was "potentially a game changer" for the Pacific.
"It was imagined by Pacific leaders. It's then been built by them. It's owned by them, and it's managed by them. And we're investing in it," Kyte said.
"What's important about it is that it can now invest in the most remote parts of the region, and it can reach the last mile."
"So not lots of intermediaries, international organisations managing money, but straight into communities."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SMJ Fellows programme to groom Sabah's future leaders
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government aims to groom a generation of high-calibre leaders through the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) Fellows Programme, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
Hajiji said the programme was more than a youth development initiative and described it as a "nursery" for Sabah's future leadership.
He said the selected fellows had the potential to lead organisations, contribute to decision-making and drive Sabah's economic development.
"I want the SMJ Fellows to see this not merely as an opportunity to gain experience, but as a responsibility to prepare themselves to become part of the generation that will take Sabah forward.
"Sabah has many intelligent, creative, courageous and ambitious young people, but some may simply need an opportunity or a mentor to help them realise their potential," he said at the presentation of appointment letters for SMJ Fellows 5.0 at Menara Kinabalu.
Hajiji said the government did not want Sabahans to leave the state simply because they could not find opportunities to excel, adding that young people should have the option of building their future in Sabah.
He said developing Sabah's human capital should also be a core commitment of government-linked companies (GLCs), which could provide young Sabahans with exposure to management, administration and the corporate sector.

Title: Govt to make viability checks mandatory for federal loans
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government plans to make viability assessments mandatory before approving new Federal Government loans, with the amount capped according to borrowers' ability to repay.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the move was aimed at strengthening the government's loan assessment model and preventing the accumulation of repayment arrears.
"The existing loan assessment model will be improved by introducing a mandatory viability assessment before any approval is given.
"Loan approvals will be capped according to the borrower's actual repayment capacity if their ability to repay is limited. The remaining project financing is proposed to be channelled in the form of grants," he said in his winding-up speech.
The proposal comes amid concerns over the government's collection of outstanding recoverable loans.
Liew said the government collected only RM465 million, or 5 per cent, of RM9.273 billion in outstanding recoverable loans in 2025.
He said RM578.32 million in repayment arrears involving 23 loans were written off during the year.
Liew said loan write-offs would only be considered after all recovery efforts, including legal action, had failed.
"Only loan interest will be considered for write-off, and only for companies confirmed to be insolvent based on a report by the Companies Commission of Malaysia, after obtaining the views of the Finance Ministry's Legal Division," he said.
