Title: Perak Perhilitan: Malayan tigers will only be captured if they threaten public safety
Article:
IPOH, Oct 7 — The Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) will only capture or translocate Malayan tigers if an assessment finds that their presence poses a threat to public safety.
Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah said the assessment takes into account the tiger’s behaviour, frequency and duration of sightings, distance from residential areas, movement patterns, and evidence of interactions or attacks involving humans or livestock.
“If the assessment shows a clear and continuing threat to human safety, Perhilitan will take appropriate action based on technical assessments in the field,” he told Bernama.
Five tiger sightings or incidents have been recorded in Perak from January to October this year, beginning with a report of a roar in Proton City, Tanjung Malim on January 10, followed by an image captured in Bukit Bangkong, Chemor on July 14 and the capture of a tigress in Hulu Kinta on July 22.
This was followed by a fatal attack in Pos Perwor, Sungai Siput on September 21 and the discovery of tiger footprints at Kem Sultan Nazrin Shah, 69 Komando, Ulu Kinta on September 29.
Pazil said tiger sightings near human settlements did not necessarily mean that their forest habitat or roaming areas were shrinking, as movements could also be influenced by prey availability, habitat conditions, human disturbance, development and land use, as well as the animals’ natural movements.
“In some situations, tigers may move through forest edges or ecological corridors within their home range and be detected near human settlements by chance,” he said.
He said Perhilitan continuously monitored prey species such as barking deer, deer and wild boar in the state’s main forest reserves, with camera traps, field surveys and population data used to assess prey availability.
Pazil said complaints about tiger sightings were assessed based on the location, time, physical evidence and current situation to determine the priority and appropriate deployment of personnel, with control teams sent to the field when there was a risk to public safety.
He said besides physical measures such as setting traps, Perhilitan also provided technical advice and safety guidance, including advising residents in high-risk areas to avoid going out alone in the early morning or late evening, refrain from provoking tigers and leave the handling of such cases to the department. — Bernama

Title: Parliament’s Palestine Caucus to submit motion on Gaza genocide for debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Malaysian Parliament’s Palestine Caucus will submit a proposed motion on the genocide in Gaza to the Office of the Dewan Rakyat Speaker and seek to have it scheduled for debate during next week’s parliamentary sitting.
Its chairman Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the proposed motion would include calls for a lasting ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and safe, sustained and unhindered access to humanitarian aid.
“Rejecting the forced displacement of Palestinians and affirming their right to self-determination, while supporting the processes of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the International Criminal Court (ICC) within their respective jurisdictions, as well as respecting relevant international judicial decisions and orders,” he said.
Syed Ibrahim, who is also Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability, said this at a press conference held in conjunction with the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide at the Parliament building here today.
The Ledang Member of Parliament also said the motion would call for efforts to strengthen diplomatic action, including scrutiny of military assistance and arms transfers that risk facilitating violations of international law.
“In addition, to establish a coordinated Malaysian framework for the recovery of Gaza, prioritising healthcare, education, child rehabilitation and Palestinian-led reconstruction,” he said.
In this regard, Syed Ibrahim said the Caucus called for sufficient time to be allocated to allow for substantive debate and the participation of Members of Parliament from across the political divide.
“To ensure the success of this initiative, the Caucus calls for coordinated engagement with the government as well as government and opposition MPs to finalise the motion and facilitate its tabling and scheduling in accordance with the Standing Orders in force,” he said.
Meanwhile, he also called on the public to participate in the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide gathering from 2pm to 5pm this Friday, which will begin at Menara Tabung Haji before proceeding to the United States Embassy. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Education Ministry orders state and district education offices, schools to monitor haze, act based on API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has instructed state education departments (JPN), district education offices (PPD) and all educational institutions under its jurisdiction to continue monitoring the current haze situation in their respective locations to determine further action.
It said the directive includes immediately suspending all outdoor activities, including outdoor gatherings and sports, particularly in areas with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings exceeding 100.
“The ministry is always monitoring the situation and prioritises the welfare, health and safety of students, especially when facing unexpected haze conditions.
“The haze situation has also resulted in several locations posting unhealthy API readings,” it said in a statement today.
It said educational institutions in the Batu Pahat district, under the supervision of the Johor JPN, are temporarily closed starting today until conditions are safe and further instructions are issued.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Batu Pahat recorded an API reading of 190 as of 10 am today.
Following the closure, home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) will be implemented based on suitability and current directives, taking into account the students’ safety, health and well-being.
“Based on the current haze situation and the latest API readings recorded nationwide, the Johor JPN has taken follow-up measures in accordance with the guidelines established by the MOE,” it added.
MOE also advised the JPN, PPD and all educational institutions under its purview to implement preventive measures outlined in the guidelines, including postponing all outdoor activities during periods of extreme heat or haze and immediately closing any school located in an area or district where the API reading exceeds 200.
It also urged schools to remain vigilant and coordinate with nearby clinics or hospitals should any students experience health complications due to the haze and hot weather.
“The JPN, PPD and all educational institutions under the MOE must also remain vigilant and monitor API readings and the latest status via the DOE’s website at https://eqms.doe.gov.my/APIMS/main on a regular basis to safeguard the health of students and the education community,” it added.
Yesterday, the Batu Pahat District Disaster Management Committee issued a directive for all schools, kindergartens and childcare centres in the district to close from today after the API reading there reached 203 as of 8pm.
The closure involved all 176 MOE-run schools in Batu Pahat, comprising 144 primary schools, 31 secondary schools and one vocational college.
Following this, state Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said in a statement that 106 state government religious schools, including  Integrated Religious Primary Schools (SRAB), and 53 registered private Islamic educational institutions (IPIS) in Batu Pahat have also been ordered to close, effective today. — Bernama

Title: Witness insists Publika office existed in Hamzah Zainudin aide’s RM350,000 corruption trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — A witness in the corruption trial involving a former political secretary to former home minister Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today maintained that the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku in Publika, the alleged location for the handover of RM350,000 in commission to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad, did exist.
Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, managing director of Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NSB), said this during cross-examination by counsel Datuk Yaacob Md Sam, appearing for Sayed Amir Muzzakkir.
Yaacob:
I put it to you that the handover of RM100,000 on December 4, 2020 and RM250,000 on December 16, 2020 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir did not take place, because the said office did not exist.
Wan Azhar:
I disagree.
In his witness statement, Wan Azhar stated that Sayed Amir Muzzakkir asked him to pay RM350,000 in cash as part of a five per cent commission, after assisting NSB secure a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) project tender.
“I handed over RM100,000 in a paper bag to Sayed around 4pm on December 4, 2020, and RM250,000, also in a paper bag, at 3.30pm on December 16, 2020. On both occasions, only Sayed and I were present,” he said in his witness statement.
The 17th prosecution witness said he had accompanied a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer to Publika to identify the said location, and found the unit in question to be closed, with no signage indicating that it was the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku.
Wan Azhar, however, disagreed with Yaacob’s suggestion that both units were vacant and unoccupied on the said dates.
Yaacob:
The owner of the premises gave evidence that, prior to the signing of the tenancy agreement, both units had been occupied by a law firm. That firm vacated the premises at the end of 2019. We therefore put it to you that from the end of 2019 until January 1, 2021, no office occupied either unit. Do you agree?
Wan Azhar:
I went to the location only twice, on December 4 and 16, 2020. I therefore know only that it was in operation on those two dates. On other days, I cannot be certain whether it was in operation or vacant.
On May 23, 2024, Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, 44, was charged on two counts of receiving RM350,000 in gratification from Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof as inducement for assisting NSB secure the RMPNet tender for PDRM valued at RM381,112,042.44.
The offences allegedly occurred at the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku, Solaris Dutamas, here, at 4pm on December 4, 2020 and at 3.30pm on December 16, 2020, respectively.
Sayed Amir Muzzakkir was also charged with soliciting RM350,000 in gratification from the same individual, for a similar purpose, at the Shah Alam office of NSB in early December 2020.
The charges were brought under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The trial before Judge Rosli Ahmad resumes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Selangor Sultan receives Silver Jubilee Keris marking 25 years on throne
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 7 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah today received the presentation of the Keris Jubli Perak, specially crafted to commemorate His Royal Highness’s 25th year on the Selangor throne.
According to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page, the ceremonial
keris
was specially commissioned as an expression of Sultan Sharafuddin’s deep appreciation for the art, heritage and diverse traditions associated with the Malay
keris
.
The
keris
was meticulously crafted to reflect the significance and uniqueness of the Sultan of Selangor’s Silver Jubilee celebrations.
Among the skilled artisans and craftsmen involved in the making of this historic
keris
were Datuk Dr Abdul Muati Zamri Ahmad, Datuk Wan Burhanuddin Wan Hassan and Datuk Mohamed Raffe Chekku, with the project led by Rafulin Foundation.
“The entire production process took 12 months, with each component crafted meticulously and in detail,” according to the post.
The Keris Jubli Perak is a symbolic work that chronicles Sultan Sharafuddin’s reign through the art of Malay heritage.
“Every material, measurement and decorative element carries its own meaning, reflecting the journey of the Sultan’s reign and the identity of Selangor.
“The
keris
measures 25 inches in length to commemorate 25 years of His Royal Highness’ reign, while the use of seven types of iron symbolises the unity of strength. The White Eagle element represents courage and authority,” the post said.
The
keris
also incorporates Black Healer wood as a symbol linking Malay heritage with traditional beliefs, while buffalo horn represents resilience and the refinement of craftsmanship.
In addition, nine gemstones are inlaid into the
keris
to represent the nine districts of Selangor.
“Twenty-five chevron-shaped motifs symbolise and commemorate the journey of His Royal Highness’ reign, spanning the past and present while carrying hopes for the future,” according to the post.
The making of the
keris
also reflects the richness of Malay heritage and the dedication of the artisans in preserving and elevating the traditional art of keris craftsmanship for future generations. — Bernama

Title: Perak MB tells accuser to prove allegations over special officer’s mosque speech
Article:
IPOH, Oct 7 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad today said that he was unsure of the veracity of an allegation that his special officer had delivered an official speech at a mosque in Kerian, stressing that the accuser must prove the claim.
Saarani said the Sultan of Perak’s decree must be obeyed and that even he, despite being the chairman of state religious affairs, would not dare to deliver a speech at any mosque.
“I am not sure about the authenticity of the activity. But if it happened, he cannot do so. To me, it is very simple — His Royal Highness’s decree must be obeyed.
“However the person making the allegation must prove it. We cannot simply make such a reckless accusation,” he told reporters after attending the closing ceremony of Perak Innovation Convention at the Stadium Indera Mulia here.
Saarani was responding to allegations that had gone viral claiming that his special officer had delivered an official speech at a programme held at a mosque in Kerian, which was alleged to have contravened the Sultan of Perak’s decree.
The allegations were made by Perak PAS Youth Strategy Director Nurhafizul Badrul Hisham via his Facebook posting, who raised questions about compliance with the Perak Sultan’s decree barring politicians from delivering speeches at mosques and surau.
Nurhafizul said the matter should be taken seriously as the ban had also been enforced through an official circular issued by the Perak Islamic Religious Department (JAIPk).
Asked about calls for an investigation and for the officer to be suspended if the allegation was proven true, Saarani said the matter also involved the chairman of the mosque committee.
“It is like this. It also involves the chairman of the mosque committee itself. Any activity that is to be held must be known to and approved by the chairman of the mosque committee.
“There have been several cases before, including one in Kuala Kangsar recently, where the matter was brought to the Islamic Religious Council for investigation, and the chairman of the mosque committee concerned was called in,” he said.
“So, if it is true the incident did happened, then we will ask the special officer concerned to apologise,” he added.

Title: Malaysia pushes to fast-track Indonesia talks on forest fire aid as haze worsens
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — Malaysia wants operational negotiations with Indonesia to be expedited to allow the country’s team to be sent to help extinguish the forest fires in that country, which have caused cross-border haze.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said that the agreement with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto regarding Malaysia’s offer of assistance has been obtained, but operational methods and the location of the Malaysian team are still under negotiation between the two countries.
“However, the way the operation will be carried out is probably being negotiated between both parties, both countries.
“I hope that the negotiations for this operation, on how and where the team from Malaysia that can help can be expedited because the haze situation in our country has become extremely severe, exceeding unhealthy levels, and is approaching the hazardous index,” he said to the media.
He said this when met after attending the graduation ceremony of the Diploma in Diplomacy Programme 2026 here today.
Mohamad said he hopes that matters related to the operation can be decided quickly so that Malaysia can send a team to help their friends in Indonesia extinguish the extensive and spreading forest fires, especially in Kalimantan.
“I personally hope that the operational issues between the two can be expedited and decided so that we can send a team to assist,” he said.
Previously, the media reported that Indonesia accepted Malaysia’s offer to help extinguish the forest fires in the republic that caused prolonged haze for several weeks.
The matter was announced by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during his working visit to Indonesia last month.
Ahmad Zahid was reported to have said that Prabowo agreed to Malaysia’s offer to help extinguish forest fires in Kalimantan, with more than 1,400 hotspots detected. — Bernama

Title: Nhaveen murder trial adjourned to tomorrow after defence seeks time over witness statements
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 7 — The High Court here today adjourned the defence proceedings of four men charged with the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen to tomorrow.
The defence sought an adjournment on the ground that it required time to follow up on the delivery of four witness statements to the prosecution today.
Judge Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid allowed the application and fixed the proceedings to resume at 9.30am tomorrow.
Counsel Maanveer Singh Dhillon, appearing for the four accused, informed the court that the defence had limited time to meet them in prison to prepare the said witness statements.
“We have just finalised the (written) witness statement. It is ready. We will deliver it to the prosecution today,” he said.
In addition, he submitted that the prosecution likewise required time to scrutinise the statements delivered today before the defence proceedings could continue.
Deputy public prosecutors Mohd Amri Johari and Yazid Mustaqim Roslan appeared for the prosecution, while the four accused were represented by counsel Maanveer Singh, R. Thevan and Lim Sheng Zhe.
On July 3, the High Court fixed October 7 to 9 and 12 to 16 for the defence trial of the four men charged with the murder of Nhaveen, nine years ago.
Previously, the Court of Appeal ordered J. Ragesuthan, 27, S. Gokulan, 27, and two other individuals who were juveniles at the time of the incident to enter their defence on the charge of murdering Nhaveen.
That decision was made after the court allowed the prosecution’s appeal against the High Court’s decision acquitting and discharging them on October 3, 2023.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code with murder, and under Section 326 of the same law with voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons, in respect of Nhaveen, 18, at the same place, date and time.
The panel of judges also directed that the case be remitted to the Penang High Court for the defence stage.
The four accused were likewise ordered to enter their defence on the charge of causing injury to Nhaveen’s friend, T. Previin, near the Karpal Singh Learning Centre on Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor, between 11pm and midnight on June 9, 2017.
Nhaveen died on June 15, 2017, from severe injuries sustained in the incident, after six days of treatment at Penang Hospital. — Bernama

Title: Sun bear still on the loose as Perhilitan widens Seremban search
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 7 — Police have stepped up patrols around Taman Tuanku Ja’afar (TTJ) after a sun bear was spotted in the residential area, with authorities widening the search as the animal remains uncaught.
Seremban district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Yatim Osman said the patrols were aimed at helping keep residents safe amid concerns that the bear could approach or attack people,
Harian Metro
reported today.
“Although this falls under the jurisdiction of the Department of Wildlife and National Parks we are also helping by patrolling the surrounding areas to detect the animal,” he said.
“At least the presence of police personnel on patrols will discourage the animal from approaching residential areas and make residents feel safer, but I advise them to remain vigilant,” he said.
The department, commonly known as Perhilitan (the Malay abbreviation of Jabatan Perlindungan Hidupan Liar dan Taman Negara), is conducting the search with the help of its personnel and members of the public, while police are assisting with efforts to safeguard residents.
Negeri Sembilan Perhilitan director Wan Mat Wan Harun said the department had widened its search after the bear failed to enter a trap set nearby.
“Perhilitan is still monitoring and tracking the bear’s movements around TTJ and nearby areas.
“For now, we are carrying out monitoring within a wider search area,” he was quoted as saying.
Wan Mat said this was the first report the department had received of a sun bear entering the TTJ residential area.
He said Perhilitan had previously received information about a sun bear at Kem 15 Rejimen Askar Melayu Diraja in Senawang, next to Taman Tuanku Ja’afar, on September 19.
“The animal was believed to have entered the residential area because it was hungry and looking for food, and the bee nests kept at the camp were raided by the bear,” he said.
The search follows a video uploaded to TikTok showing the animal tearing into the roof of a hut in the housing area at about midnight last Sunday.
The sun bear is the world’s smallest bear species and is native to South-east Asia, including Malaysia.
It is classified as vulnerable on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List, with its population declining due mainly to habitat loss, hunting and human-bear conflict.
As a forest-dependent animal, sun bears can occasionally venture into human settlements in search of food, bringing them into potentially dangerous encounters with residents.

Title: Two senior students to face murder charge tomorrow over Kuala Pilah sports school death
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 7 — Two 16-year-old boys suspected of involvement in the death of a younger boy at a sports school in Kuala Pilah last month are expected to be charged with murder tomorrow, Berita Harian reported.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the investigation papers had been referred to the state prosecution office.
“Both suspects will be brought to the Kuala Pilah Magistrate’s Court at 9.30am tomorrow,” he was quoted as saying.
He said the prosecution had instructed that both suspects be charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which deals with acts done by several people with a common intention.
According to media reports at the time, the 14-year-old was found unconscious at the school hostel at about 8pm on September 25.
He was taken to Hospital Tuanku Ampuan Najihah in Kuala Pilah, where he was pronounced dead.
His body was then sent to the forensic medicine department at Hospital Tuanku Ja’afar in Seremban for a post-mortem.
Police subsequently detained two 16-year-old boys, who are seniors of the victim, to assist investigations and classified the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Alzafny previously said the remand of the first suspect is extended until tomorrow, while the second suspect’s remand is extended until October 9.

Title: Higher Education Ministry says institutions given autonomy to adjust learning mode when API exceeds 201
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — Higher education institutions (IPTs) in areas recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 201 have been given the flexibility to determine suitable teaching and learning (PdP) modes to reduce health risks while ensuring students’ education continues
In a statement today, the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) said it was closely monitoring air quality and had directed all institutions under its purview to monitor API readings in their respective areas.
Outdoor activities should also be assessed and adjusted according to the latest readings.
The ministry advised IPT communities to refer to official information from the Department of Environment (DOE) and follow the guidelines issued by their respective institutions.
“MOHE will continue to monitor the situation and adjust the operations of IPTs to safeguard the health, well-being and welfare of all its members,” it said.
Bernama reported that 35 areas recorded unhealthy API readings as of 10 am today.
According to the DOE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Batu Pahat, Johor, and Johan Setia, Selangor recorded the highest readings at 190 each, followed by Cheras, Kuala Lumpur, and Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, at 189 each, and Putrajaya at 187.
API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Two corporate figures with 'Datuk Seri’, 'Datuk Wira’ titles out on MACC bail
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Two corporate figures, who are brothers holding the titles of Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira and who were previously remanded for five days to assist investigations into abuse of power and irregularities involving an investment of about RM10 million, have been released on Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) bail.
According to MACC sources, the suspect with the ‘Datuk Wira’ title was released on Monday (Oct 5) after his remand period ended.
“The other suspect, with the ‘Datuk Seri’ title, was released today after his remand period, which was extended by two days, ended,” the sources added.
On Oct 1, both men, in their 40s and 50s, were remanded for five days after being detained on Sept 30 when they turned up to give their statements at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.
The sources said the MACC also seized 15 luxury cars worth about RM31 million, 12 high-powered motorcycles valued at about RM5 million, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash, in addition to freezing two personal bank accounts containing about RM2 million.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed the matter. — Bernama

Title: ‘I was both her mother and friend’: Zara Qairina’s mother tells inquest
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 7 —The mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir testified at the Coroner’s Court today that she was the teenager’s principal confidante, to whom her daughter confided her troubles, joys, sorrows and matters concerning her friendships.
Noraidah Lamat, 46, the 82nd witness, testified that their bond was especially close and that she was not only a mother but also a friend to her only child.
“My relationship with Zara Qairina was indeed close. I was both her mother and friend. Whatever the matter, be it difficulties at school or amusing incidents, we would share everything,” she said during the inquest proceedings before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
She said no one else in the household was a confidante for Zara Qairina, and accordingly, her daughter shared all her joys, sorrows and friendship matters with her.
During questioning by her counsel, Shahlan Jufri, Noraidah testified that she had attended to almost all of Zara Qairina’s needs since childhood, including preparing for school, clothing, religious school, homework and school-related affairs.
She testified that this was because Zara Qairina’s father, Mahathir Mohd Hashim @ Marikan, worked in Sipitang and was seldom at home, so she had to manage their child’s care, schooling, expenses, and welfare.
She stated that their close relationship also enabled her to discern shifts in Zara Qairina’s emotional state through what her daughter told her about her friendships, including occasions when the girl faced taunting.
Throughout Zara Qairina’s years in primary school, Noraidah testified that she had never observed her daughter suffering any serious emotional or behavioural difficulties.
She said when Zara Qairina was sad or disappointed, it usually related to a falling-out with a friend or to some incident in her daily life.
In such circumstances, Noraidah said she would offer words of encouragement and remind Zara Qairina that there are still opportunities for self-improvement.
Noraidah further testified that Zara Qairina had, from the outset, been eager to stay in the hostel, wishing to experience independent living and to have companions as well as senior students whom she could regard as elder sisters.
She said Zara Qairina was excited upon receiving the offer of admission to the boarding school, and that they had made preparations together, including buying clothes and other necessities.
The day she sent Zara Qairina to the hostel on Feb 18, 2025, was also the first time Noraidah had been apart from her only child.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after the Form One student was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel at 4 am.
The inquest proceedings resume later this afternoon. — Bernama

Title: Air quality deteriorates as 37 stations enter unhealthy bracket, Klang Valley and Johor hard hit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated further late this afternoon, with 37 monitoring stations nationwide recording readings in the unhealthy bracket as of 4.30pm, according to Department of Environment (DoE) surveillance data.
The figure marks an increase from the 32 affected stations reported during the department’s 9am morning update.
Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the nation’s highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 190, holding steady from its morning level and remaining just ten points shy of the 201 threshold that triggers a “very unhealthy” categorisation.
Cheras in Kuala Lumpur followed closely behind with an API reading of 187, while Nilai in Negeri Sembilan registered 185, Putrajaya posted 183, and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 180.
Batu Pahat in Johor, which logged the country’s worst air quality at 197 in the morning, showed modest improvement by late afternoon, easing to 179 to rank sixth nationwide.
Greater Klang Valley shrouded in smog
The Greater Klang Valley urban belt saw extensive haze coverage, accounting for nine unhealthy stations across Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya.
In Selangor, six stations logged elevated pollution levels. Beyond Johan Setia, unhealthy air quality was recorded in Shah Alam (177), Petaling Jaya (174), Banting (172), Klang (170), and Kuala Selangor (153).
In the Federal Territories, both Kuala Lumpur stations remained in the high unhealthy range with Cheras at 187 and Batu Muda at 180, while the administrative centre of Putrajaya stood at 183.
Johor recorded the highest number of affected monitoring points of any state, with eight stations in the unhealthy band. Following Batu Pahat, elevated readings were registered in Segamat (178), Pasir Gudang (176), Larkin (172), Tangkak (169), Pengerang (166), Kota Tinggi (166), and Kluang (164).
In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai led with 185, followed by the state capital Seremban at 175 and coastal Port Dickson at 166.
All three monitoring stations in Melaka recorded unhealthy conditions: Bukit Rambai (176), Bandaraya Melaka (174), and Alor Gajah (172).
On the east coast of the peninsula, Pahang logged five affected locations, comprising Rompin (165), Temerloh (164), Indera Mahkota in Kuantan (159), Balok Baru in Kuantan (155), and Jerantut, which improved markedly to 105 from 159 in the morning.
In Terengganu, industrial hubs Kemaman and Paka both registered 153, while state capital Kuala Terengganu logged 134.
In Perak, four stations remained in the unhealthy category: Tasek Ipoh at 155 (down from 174 at 9am), Seri Manjung and Tanjung Malim tied at 154, and Pegoh Ipoh at 151.
Elsewhere, Tawau in Sabah registered 156, while Sungai Petani in Kedah logged the lowest reading on the national unhealthy list at 107.
Under the DoE’s API scale, readings between 0 and 50 are categorized as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous.

Title: Revoked excos fight back: Ten ask High Court to void Negeri Sembilan gazette
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Ten Negeri Sembilan state executive councillors (excos) have sued the state government in the High Court to challenge the revocation of their appointments, their lawyers said today.
They want the court to declare that the revocation, gazetted on September 24, is invalid.
In a statement, law firm Hafarizam Wan & Aisha Mubarak said the 10 filed the lawsuit on October 5 by originating summons at the High Court in Seremban.
The defendants are the Negeri Sembilan government and the state secretary.
The lawyers said the 10 had filed 10 affidavits in support, while Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ismail Lasim had also filed an additional affidavit.
“We ask that the public not make any speculation related to this originating summons until it is disposed by the court to prevent sub judice matters from arising,” the firm said.
Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, revoked the appointments after stating that the 10 had breached their oath of loyalty, according to the gazette.
The gazette said the revocation took effect on September 20 and was made under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959, which says an exco member other than the Menteri Besar holds office at the Ruler's pleasure.
Ismail has said he was not consulted on the revocation, and that the constitution provides for such a revocation only on the Menteri Besar’s advice.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has said the revocation is valid because exco members other than the Menteri Besar hold office at the Ruler’s pleasure.
The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umairah Hashim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
In their statement, the lawyers described them as excos and did not use the term “former excos”.
In a court document seen by
Malay Mail
today, the 10 are seeking 12 court orders.
They include a declaration that the power to revoke an exco’s appointment must follow the requirements and procedures in the state constitution.
They also seek declarations that the Ruler cannot revoke an exco’s appointment on his own, or at his pleasure alone, without the menteri besar’s advice.
Because the constitution requires the menteri besar’s advice for such a revocation, they argue, the gazette revoking their appointments without it was “null, void and ineffective”.
They also want a direct declaration that the revocation, which was gazetted by the state secretary, is invalid.
The 10 further want the High Court to give directions for an expedited hearing.
They also want compensation in the form of general, exemplary and aggravated damages, with the amount to be decided by the court.
Recommended reading:
N. Sembilan Ruler formally revokes appointments of 10 exco members
* An earlier version of this article contained an error which has since been rectified.

Title: Seven suspects: Chinese national latest held as Pahang police close in on RM1.7m Genting jewellery heist
Article:
BENTONG, Oct 7 — A Chinese national in his 40s became the latest suspect arrested over the RM1.7 million jewellery heist at SkyAvenue, Genting Highlands, bringing the total number of arrests to seven.
The man was detained after arriving at Kuala Lumpur International Airport yesterday and has been remanded until October 10 to assist police investigations,
The New Straits Times
reported today.
“The man has been remanded until October 10 to assist investigations. We did not recover any items related to the case.
“Police have so far arrested five foreigners and two locals,” Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob was quoted as saying.
He said none of the items reported stolen have been recovered  from the suspect so far.
Police are still tracking down the remaining suspects, he added.
The heist took place on August 17, when three masked men armed with an axe and crowbars broke into a goldsmith shop at the hilltop resort before fleeing with jewellery worth about RM1.7 million.
Closed-circuit television footage showed the suspects, wearing caps, face masks and jackets, arriving at the resort in a vehicle before carrying out the robbery.

Title: Some money in an account is linked to crime, can govt take all of it? Court of Appeal says no
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — When money from an investment scam landed in a company’s bank account, the government moved to seize everything in it, but the Court of Appeal has now drawn a line on how far such confiscation can go.
A three-judge panel ruled that authorities can take money proven to be linked to a crime, but cannot automatically seize the rest of the money in the same account without evidence connecting it to the offence, news outlet
Free Malaysia Today
(
FMT
) reported today.
The ruling came after LWC Good Service Sdn Bhd challenged a High Court order allowing the government to forfeit RM1.36 million from two of its bank accounts under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Amla).
The prosecution was able to trace RM360,000 directly from a bank account linked to the Comoncaps investment scam into LWC’s Hong Leong Bank account, according to the
FMT
report.
But the court found there was no evidence showing that the rest of the money in LWC’s accounts came from the scam.
As such, the panel comprising Datuk Azman Abdullah, Dean Wayne Daly and chaired by K. Muniandy, ordered the RM360,000 to be forfeited, while directing that RM863,179.84 in the Hong Leong Bank account and RM139,329.24 in LWC’s CIMB account be returned to the company.
In delivering the unanimous judgment, Muniandy said suspicion alone was not enough to justify taking money that had not been proven to be linked to criminal activity,
FMT
reported.
“Suspicion, however compelling or grave, does not take the place of legal proof,” he was quoted as saying in the written grounds.
The judge said Amla could not be turned into a broad tool for confiscating money simply because a company had irregularities or dealt with business partners who failed to comply with financial requirements.
In simple terms, the court said the money that could be traced to the scam had to be separated from the rest rather than treating the entire bank account as criminal proceeds.
LWC was among 28 respondents in civil forfeiture proceedings arising from the Comoncaps investment fraud, in which 22 victims allegedly lost about RM3.49 million.
The High Court had previously ordered the entire balance of RM1.223 million in LWC’s Hong Leong Bank account and RM139,329.24 in its CIMB account to be forfeited.
The Court of Appeal said the High Court had erred by failing to distinguish the RM360,000 that was proven to be linked to the scam from the remaining funds, according to
FMT.

Title: National Unity Ministry to study effectiveness of existing 3R, hate speech laws
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — The National Unity Ministry, through the Unity Issues Management Committee (JPIP), will undertake a comprehensive review of the effectiveness of existing legal provisions and enforcement mechanisms in addressing issues related to religion, royalty and race (3R), as well as hate speech.
In a statement today, the ministry said the matters to be reviewed included the definitions of 3R and hate speech, jurisdictional scope, overlapping legal provisions and the effectiveness of enforcement actions under existing laws.
The committee will be co-chaired by National Unity Ministry secretary-general Datuk Haslina Abdul Hamid, Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, and Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) director-general at the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Zamri Misman.
“The ministry acknowledges that various legal provisions are already in place to address issues related to 3R, hate speech and social harmony.
“These include the Sedition Act 1948, Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, Printing Presses and Publications Act 1984, as well as relevant provisions under the Penal Code which fall under the purview of the Home Ministry and the Communications Ministry,” the statement read.
The ministry said the prohibition against discrimination is already provided for under Article 8 of the Federal Constitution, which serves as the country’s supreme law.
Therefore, it said any proposal to establish an additional institution or introduce new legislation must be assessed comprehensively to avoid overlapping functions, jurisdictions and enforcement mechanisms.
“The ministry is of the view that the main challenge is not the absence of legal provisions on 3R issues, but ensuring the firm and consistent enforcement of existing provisions,” the statement read.
It therefore said the government, through a cross-agency approach, needed to comprehensively review the effectiveness of existing enforcement mechanisms, including identifying weaknesses, gaps and constraints in the enforcement process, and strengthen the relevant mechanisms.
In addition, the ministry said it would hold further discussions with the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) to ensure greater clarity on roles and more effective coordination in addressing issues concerning social harmony.
“The ministry will also propose to Suhakam the appointment of a Harmony Commissioner to focus specifically on monitoring and advocating for social harmony from a human rights perspective,” it said.
The statement said the ministry, through the Department of National Unity and Integration (JPNIN), would also develop an Action Plan to Strengthen the National Social Harmony Ecosystem, integrating prevention, early intervention, mediation, enforcement and monitoring in a more structured and cohesive manner. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: Follow-up action on audits generates over RM920m in government revenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Follow-up action on audits by the National Audit Department has contributed to revenue collection and repayments to the government amounting to RM920.91 million as at Sept 28, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the figure demonstrated the effectiveness of audits when identified findings were followed by appropriate action.
“This is not a small amount. It proves that audits followed by action can result in tangible recovery of public funds,” she said when tabling a motion on the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Azalina said all ministries, departments and agencies should not view audit findings as “an attack”, but rather as an opportunity to rectify weaknesses, improve systems and safeguard public funds.
She said LKAN 2/2026, which was tabled on Oct 5, comprises two main volumes covering the 2025 Federal Government Financial Statements and a performance audit of four ministry, department and agency programmes or activities.
According to Azalina, 38 recommendations were made in the report, with follow-up action required to address questions concerning the parties responsible, corrective measures, completion timelines and methods for monitoring progress.
As such, she said the debate on the LKAN in the Dewan Rakyat was important to ensure that accountability did not end after an audit report was tabled.
“Audit must lead to action. Findings must lead to corrective measures. Weaknesses must lead to improvements,” she said.
She also called on state legislative assemblies to provide room for the LKAN to be examined and debated openly, rather than merely being tabled for information, to ensure that the principle of accountability is applied at every level of government.
Azalina also said amendments to the Audit Act 1957 in 2024 had strengthened the institution of the Auditor General, including through an expanded audit scope, the Follow the Public Money Audit approach, powers to issue audit guidelines and conduct follow-up audits.
She said institutional reform initiatives, including freedom of information, political financing reform and the establishment of the Malaysian Ombudsman, complemented the audit function by emphasising prevention, transparency and accountability from the outset. — Bernama

Title: Tax-exempt taxpayers can opt to keep using e-invoices, says Liew
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 —Approximately 160,000 taxpayers who have registered for e-Invoicing but are now exempted can choose whether to continue using the system or not.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said they are part of the 1.1 million taxpayers among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of RM3 million or below, who are now exempt from implementing e-Invoicing.
However, Liew said a total of 164,435 taxpayers in this category had opted to implement e-Invoicing voluntarily.
“They can choose to continue, or they can choose not to continue,” he said when answering a supplementary question in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau), who wanted to know the number of business entities or companies exempted from implementing e-Invoicing, as well as the estimated impact of the exemption on the country’s potential tax revenue.
Beginning Sept 1, 2026, the government announced that MSMEs with annual income or sales of less than RM3 million would not be required to implement e-Invoicing.
Liew said some of the challenges faced by MSMEs include tax compliance, the transition from physical stores to online platforms, and competition from other countries.
He said the government is taking and will continue to take steps to reduce the bureaucratic burden and ensure that MSMEs are not overburdened by e-Invoicing compliance requirements and other challenges they have faced following the Covid-19 pandemic.
Meanwhile, Liew said companies with annual sales exceeding RM100 million began implementing e-Invoicing on Aug 1, 2024, involving 5,578 taxpayers.
He said the implementation was subsequently expanded to companies with annual sales between RM25 million and RM100 million, involving 14,567 taxpayers; companies with sales between RM5 million and RM25 million, involving 51,710 taxpayers; and companies with sales between RM3 million and RM5 million, involving 25,503 taxpayers. — Bernama

Title: Repatriation among key issues as Myanmar president arrives in Malaysia
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 7 — Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing arrived in Malaysia today for a two-day official visit, with the repatriation of Myanmar nationals in Malaysia among key issues to be discussed with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The special aircraft carrying Min and his delegation touched down at the Bunga Raya Complex of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) at 12.30 pm.
Upon arrival, he was accorded a static guard of honour mounted by two officers and 26 personnel of various ranks from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment, led by Capt Muhammad Ikhwan Adlan Jamaludin.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, the minister-in-attendance, was at the airport to welcome the Myanmar leader.
Also present were Malaysian Government Chief Protocol Officer Datuk Rozainor Ramli and Charge d’Affaires of Malaysia to Myanmar Johan Ariff Abdul Razak.
On Thursday, Min will be accorded an official welcoming ceremony at the Perdana Putra Complex in Putrajaya, followed by a bilateral meeting with Anwar and an official luncheon hosted by the Prime Minister.
Wisma Putra said the visit would also provide the Prime Minister with an opportunity to sustain his direct engagement with Myanmar, in line with the decision of the 48th ASEAN Summit in May 2026 to continue constructive and principled engagement with Myanmar.
It said Myanmar is an integral part of ASEAN, and Malaysia, as a fellow member state, will continue to support the bloc’s efforts to promote peace, reconciliation and access to humanitarian assistance in the country.
Malaysia will also work closely with all ASEAN member states to ensure stability and prosperity in the region. — Bernama

Title: Disputed Undang abandon case to depose Negeri Sembilan Yamtuan, cannot refile lawsuit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Four Undangs or traditional ruling chiefs of Negeri Sembilan — including three disputed ones — today dropped their court attempt in Kuala Lumpur to ultimately remove Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Negeri Sembilan ruler.
Today, the four men — Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Datuk Muhammed Abdullah and Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin — applied to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur to withdraw their court case against the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar and the Negeri Sembilan state government.
In their court case filed in July via judicial review, the four men had wanted the court to order the Menteri Besar to sign — within seven days of the court order — their April 19 declaration to “sack” Tuanku Muhriz as Negeri Sembilan ruler.
The April 19 declaration document also contains the four men's declaration that they had selected and appointed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the new Negeri Sembilan ruler.
They had also wanted the court to declare that the April 19 declaration is a valid document according to the Negeri Sembilan state constitution.
But after the four men applied to drop the case, the High Court in Kuala Lumpur today also decided that the dropped case cannot be filed again.
When contacted, lawyer Steven Thiru confirmed to Malay Mail that the four men had dropped the case in the Kuala Lumpur courts, but said they did not give any reason to the court for the case withdrawal.
Steven was representing the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) and the DKU secretary, two of the proposed interveners to the case.
There were four proposed interveners or four parties who were applying to join the court case, namely the DKU, DKU secretary, the current Sungei Ujong Undang Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and current Rembau Undang Datuk Hassan Ab. Hamid.
In explaining what happened in open court today before High Court judge Norliza Othman, Steven said the four men had asked to withdraw the court case with no order on legal costs, while the Attorney-General’s Chambers had agreed to the withdrawal with no order as to costs.
Steven said that the four proposed interveners did not object to the withdrawal, but had asked the court to give order on costs, as the withdrawal of the judicial review would mean that the case had no merits.
“Importantly, the judicial review in the Kuala Lumpur High Court was an abuse of process,” he told Malay Mail.
Steven said the four men’s court case was an abuse of court process, as they did not disclose these key facts to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur: that there was a pending court proceeding in the High Court in Seremban that they had already started with two other individuals, as well as the High Court in Seremban’s June 5 injunction order and July 8 order for leave for contempt of court which the DKU and DKU secretary had obtained.
Steven said the four men’s act of filing a court case in Kuala Lumpur on July 17 when they already had an ongoing case in Seremban amounted to “forum shopping”.
“Forum shopping” is known as the act of shopping around or looking for a court which would most likely decide in their favour.
“This was a clear case of forum shopping, as well as suppression of material facts from the Kuala Lumpur High Court in the judicial review which was filed on July 17, 2026,” he said.
Steven said the High Court today ultimately ordered the four men to pay RM40,000 in costs, namely RM10,000 to each of the four proposed interveners.
He also confirmed that the High Court decided that the four have no liberty to file afresh or cannot file the same court case again.
On August 1, the DKU announced that these three individuals — Mubarak, Abdul Rahim, and Maarof — had either ceased to hold or never lawfully held the positions of Undang for Sungei Ujong, Rembau and Jelebu.
The four men in today’s court are those three individuals, as well as Muhammed who is currently listed as the Johol Undang on the Negeri Sembilan state government’s website.
On August 1, the DKU formally recognised Muhammad Faris and Raja Hassan as the Undang for Sungei Ujong and Rembau, and said Maarof had been dismissed as Jelebu Undang.
The Negeri Sembilan state government’s website currently lists the Jelebu Undang position as vacant.

Title: Melaka state election set for Nov 14 polling, Oct 31 nomination
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 7 — The Election Commission (EC) today announced November 14 for polling in the 16th Melaka state election, and set the nomination for Oct 31.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said early voting had been set for November 10 and the campaign period would run for 14 days.
He said this at a press conference after chairing a special meeting to determine the date for the state election here.
Regarding the Electoral Roll (DPPR) that will be used in the 16th Melaka state election (PRN), Ramlan said that a total of 687,697 voters, consisting of 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel, are eligible to vote in the state election.
For postal voting matters, applications for both domestic and international categories have been open since Sept 23, and the deadline for postal voting applications for Category 1A, which includes election staff, EC officers, military personnel, and media, is set for Oct 28.
“For Category 1B, which is Malaysian citizens abroad, and 1C, which is for agencies or organisations, the deadline is on Oct 23,” he said.
Commenting further, Ramlan said the EC appointed 28 returning officers and 80 assistant returning officers.
He said that to monitor election campaign activities throughout the official campaigning period, the EC will establish 28 Election Campaign Enforcement Teams (PP-KPR), including representatives from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), local authorities (PBT), and representatives of contesting candidates.
“A total of 28 candidate nomination centres (PPC) and official vote counting centres (PPRU) will be used in this election, while 11,175 personnel will be appointed to manage the process.
“A total of 271 polling centres with 1,263 channels will be opened, involving 31 early voting centres with 50 early voting channels and 240 regular polling centres with 1,213 channels,” he said, adding that the allocation for conducting the Melaka state election is estimated at RM28.45 million.
He said the EC is also offering government agencies and non-governmental organisations (NGO) to be election observers to monitor the Melaka state election process from nomination day until the election results are announced.
“They are allowed to make observations at the PPC, polling centres, counting centres and PPRU, and must comply with all the appointment conditions set by the EC.”
Further information and application forms related to election observers can be obtained from the SPR Portal
www.spr.gov.my
starting from Oct 7, 2026 (today) and until Oct 21, 2026. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Lim Guan Eng urges caution on foreign worker wage hikes over SME contract risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Federal lawmaker Lim Guan Eng (Bagan - DAP) today again called on the government to consider the financial impact on small and medium businesses amid rumours it could raise the minimum wage when tabling Budget 2027, warning that abrupt hikes could disrupt long-term commercial agreements.
Lim, a former finance minister, argued that many enterprises operate under binding multi-year contracts where labor costs are fixed at agreed-upon rates.
“Many businesses have long-term contracts with foreign workers at agreed rates,” the DAP leader said at a press conference in Parliament this afternoon.
“A sudden wage increase would place an unexpected financial burden on employers.”
Lim, a former finance minister, noted that unexpected cost surges could strain operating margins and create operational friction for businesses unable to renegotiate existing contractual terms on short notice.
The former minister has been vocal in opposing the minimum wage hike and mandatory EPF contribution for foreign workers.
Lim claimed employers are often forced to hire foreign workers because it’s difficult to hire locals, particularly for SMEs, although his critics reject the argument as a “script” companies typically deploy to continue suppressing wages.
The former minister’s view closely aligns with the core arguments consistently raised by the Malaysian Employers Federation. The MEF generally opposes frequent or steep statutory minimum wage hikes across the board, favoring wage growth tied strictly “to productivity and market forces”.
Malaysian workers productivity have grown in the last 10 years, yet real wages grew at a fraction of that rate — averaging around 1 per cent annually, with periods of stagnant or declining purchasing power for private-sector employees, data from Bank Negara Malaysia and the Department of Statistics Malaysia showed.
Malaysia’s compensation of employees (CE) share of GDP, that is the portion of economic output paid out as wages, has historically lingered around 32 to 35 per cent, significantly below developed economies, data from the two bodies show.
This means greater share of value creation by Malaysian workers flows to capital returns, corporate profits, and reinvestment rather than payroll.
CE typically sits between 45 to 50 per cent in richer economies.

Title: A bridge, fresh paint and ‘like Deepavali’: Wangsa Sari PPR in KL gets a makeover
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The park is just across Sungai Bonus, but for children at the Wangsa Sari People's Housing Programme here, getting there has meant balancing along water pipes.
By the end of this year, they should be able to simply walk across, with an 18-metre-long, two-metre-wide pedestrian bridge expected to be completed behind the 21-storey block.
It will lead to Padang Wangsa Sari and reduce the need for residents to use the narrower Jalan 2/27A.
Resident Mohd Fazil Md Noor, 56, said it would also give children a safer and easier way to get to SK Wangsa Maju Section 1, where some currently walk or cycle.
“We really need the bridge that is going to be built because once it is completed, it will become the main route for our children to get to and from school.
“The school is less than 5km from this PPR. If they cross the bridge, it will be much closer, perhaps cutting about 1km off the journey. Some of our children walk or cycle to school, so building this bridge is really ideal. This is something we have been hoping for,” he told
Malay Mail
when met today.
The idea began when Wangsa Maju MP Zahir Hassan visited the area in 2023 and found that residents of the flats had limited access to recreational facilities despite a park being across the river.
Wangsa Sari PPR resident Jasbee Kaur, 67, speaks to Malay Mail about the planned pedestrian bridge and the facelift. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
“After winning the 2022 general election, when I came here in 2023, we walked around the area and found that there were not enough facilities.
“We saw that there was a park across the river and asked how we could make maximum use of the park,” he told
Malay Mail
during a visit today.
Zahir said he later raised the matter with Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Fadlun Mak Ujud, after learning that children had fallen into the river while attempting to cross using the water pipes.
“When the children had fallen, they did not think of it as a tragedy because they fell into the water, but it was dangerous. We were worried about what would happen if the water level was high,” he said.
Fadlun said Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) had allocated an additional RM200,000 for the bridge and would try to expedite its construction for completion before the end of the year.
Once complete, the bridge is expected to serve all 1,061 residents and encourage greater use of the park for exercise and community activities.
Another resident, Jasbee Kaur, 67, who has lived at the Wangsa Sari flats – commonly known by the abbreviation PPR for Projek Perumahan Rakyat – for 19 years, said residents had welcomed the bridge, which she believed would make it easier for children to return home from the park.
“The bridge is needed. When the children are tired, they will have a shortcut to come home and it will be easier for them to enter the taman next door,” she said.
However, 53-year-old resident Nurazlina Abd Aziz said safety concerns would remain once the bridge is completed, particularly with motorcycles parked behind the block.
“Many motorcycles are parked at the back, so there may be an increase in theft. If the children want to go to school, yes, but we also have to think about their safety,” she said.
The bridge is part of a wider facelift for Wangsa Sari PPR, which was built in 2008 and has 272 residential units housing about 1,061 residents.
The block, previously painted entirely white, now has a two-tone beige and white colour scheme under a RM2.24 million upgrading project covering the building and its basic infrastructure.
Of the allocation, RM1.1 million was spent on repainting the building, RM904,000 on replacing the sub-main cable and main switchboard, RM136,000 on road resurfacing and RM101,000 on upgrading the fire safety system.
Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said one of the reforms introduced was allowing MPs, through a committee set up to monitor DBKL spending, to provide feedback on how the city hall allocates funds.
“With feedback from all these MPs, our spending is more transparent and also meets the needs of residents. So, we do not have wasteful expenditure because all of this involves basic infrastructure needed by residents,” she said.
She said the repainting was also intended to improve the dignity of PPR residents, with the new neutral colour scheme selected by Fadlun.
“I agree that PPR buildings are usually painted in too many colours, to the point that they look like kindergartens. But now, all the colours are neutral and look nice,” she said.
Fadlun said DBKL had completed almost 70 per cent of upgrading projects involving the city’s 64 PPR and public housing schemes under the RM300 million allocation this year.
He said expenditure was expected to reach 90 per cent of the allocation by year-end, with about RM23 million to be carried forward to complete the remaining projects.
Fazil, who has lived at the PPR for about 15 years, said the makeover felt like a festive occasion.
“Our buildings have also been repainted. It feels like Hari Raya, everything looks new, Alhamdulillah. The wiring and lights have also been replaced, and we have seen the improvements,” he said.
Jasbee, asked about Fazil’s Hari Raya description, laughed and gave the makeover her own festive comparison.
“For me, it’s like Deepavali!” she said.
She said the improvements had also brought a renewed sense of community among residents, whom she described as cooperative and supportive of one another.
“Our residents are very cooperative. We stick with each other,” she said.
Still, she has one request for the government.
“We want the government to open up the opportunity for us to buy these homes. We are still renting them. We need to be able to buy them,” she said.

Title: Azalina sees ‘dangerous misogynistic tendency’ in violence against female students, urges closer look
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said today said the recent fatal attacks on female students in schools and universities could signal a rise in misogyny, and called for the underlying causes to be examined in depth.
Speaking to reporters in Parliament, she said many of the victims were women targeted by people they knew, such as classmates or faculty mates.
“From what I have observed generally, many of the victims are women, and those committing these acts are people they know — perhaps classmates or faculty mates,” she said.
“So it seems as though there is an element of gender-based violence. Whether the response stems from rejection, jealousy, and so on, what concerns me is that women are becoming victims of violence in these situations.”
Her remarks come after the death of 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Khairoul Faisal, who was found dead in her school hall after failing to return home from extra classes.
Police said she suffered fatal blunt force trauma to the head, and have remanded three male schoolmates to assist with investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
Azalina said the attacks appeared to be driven by a sense of entitlement, where being refused or rejected is met with violence.
“This matter needs to be examined in depth because it seems as though these acts can be committed because of a sense of entitlement. When someone asks for something and doesn’t get it, or wants something and is denied it, the response is violence.
“This is a very dangerous misogynistic tendency,” she added.
She added that female students were bearing the brunt of such aggression, and stressed the need for monitoring and intervention across the ministries responsible.
Azalina also pointed to a wider cultural shift, saying young people have grown impatient and expect things to arrive quickly, citing app-based delivery services.
“Young people today want everything quickly. In the past, if you wanted to cook, you had to look for onions, chop the vegetables, right? Today you just call Grab and everything arrives,” she said.
“You want a headset, you order by phone and it arrives. It cannot continue like this… this is why I feel this issue must be looked into seriously.”

Title: No warnings, just arrests: Mayor says this is how DBKL deals with parking touts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) does not issue notices to parking touts and simply arrests those caught during operations, mayor Datuk Fadlun Mak Ujud said today.
He said 84 touts, commonly called “ulat parking” in Malay, had been arrested in operations carried out at 49 locations around the capital.
“We do not issue notices. We just arrest them. When we conduct an operation and find them, we arrest them,” he told reporters after visiting the  Wangsa Sari flats under the People’s Housing Programme here.
Fadlun said the operations are ongoing, but that the touts sometimes flee when enforcement officers arrive.
“At times, when our enforcement officers arrive, they run away,” he said.
The issue resurfaced on social media recently after a video went viral showing an alleged parking tout confronting a motorist over payment.
It has renewed calls for firmer action against touts who approach motorists and demand payment where there is no official parking charge.
In August, Seputeh MP Teresa Kok shared a video of the arrest of an alleged illegal parking collector along Jalan Hujan in Taman OUG.
The man was arrested after he allegedly repeatedly ignored enforcement notices and assaulted an enforcement officer during a confrontation.
He was also alleged to have continued collecting parking fees despite enforcement action by DBKL and other authorities.

Title: Malaysia’s Gen Z leads surge in support for banning children from social media, Ipsos poll finds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Gen Z Malaysians, the first generation raised entirely in the digital age, are increasingly spearheading calls to keep children off social media, according to a new survey by global market research firm Ipsos.
The study revealed that 81 per cent of Gen Z respondents in Malaysia agree that children under the age of 14 should be barred from social media platforms both during and outside school hours, marking a sharp jump from 67 per cent recorded a year earlier. This represents the steepest increase in support across any demographic group surveyed.
Support among older cohorts also trended upwards. Gen X backing rose by 13 percentage points to 86 per cent, while Millennial support climbed six points to 85 per cent. Overall, 83 per cent of Malaysian adults now endorse an under-14 ban, up from 72 per cent in 2025.
The findings place Malaysia second among 31 countries surveyed globally in backing social media age curbs, trailing only Indonesia (90 per cent) and well above the global average of 73 per cent.
“[Gen Z] that grew up with social media appears to understand its downsides firsthand, and to recognise that today's children face greater risks than they once did, as AI deepfakes and misinformation blur the line between what is real and what is not,” Ipsos said in its analysis of the data.
The survey polled adults aged 18 to 74, meaning the Gen Z demographic reflects the perspectives of young adults reflecting on their own online upbringing rather than the children directly affected.
Regulatory safeguards underway
The survey coincides with heightened national scrutiny over online safety after Malaysia began enforcing comprehensive regulatory safeguards on June 1.
Under the new licensing framework, major platforms with at least eight million domestic users, including Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok, and YouTube, must implement robust age-verification systems to prevent underage account creation.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) said that the regulatory measures are designed to enhance platform accountability.
MCMC deputy director for development Eneng Faridah Iskandar stated on CNA+'s Talking Point on Aug 6 that technology firms deploying commercial products in the open market carry a duty of care to ensure user safety and identify who accesses their services.
She noted that the regulator has documented evidence of minors experiencing online harm, exploitation, and abuse, citing MCMC figures indicating that 70 per cent of Malaysian teenagers have already encountered harmful online material.
Regional approaches to online safety
Ipsos highlighted that age restrictions alone cannot serve as a complete solution, noting that long-term efficacy depends on collaborative enforcement among tech platforms, parents, and educators. The global conversation is progressively pivoting from whether children should have internet access to establishing structured, protective environments.
Across Southeast Asia, regulatory frameworks vary widely. Singapore is preparing enhanced statutory safeguards for users under 18 without implementing a blanket ban, receiving 74 per cent public support. Thailand is evaluating age-based restrictions, registering 54 per cent public backing.
The Malaysian study sampled 501 adults online between June 19 and July 3, including 207 Gen Z respondents. Subgroup breakdowns carry wider margins of error than national-level figures.

Title: Flying in to KLIA after midnight? Buses replace Aerotrain from 12am to 5am during software works
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 7 — The KLIA Aerotrain will be paused from 12am to 5am during two rounds of software works in October and November, with buses taking over transfers between the Main Terminal and Satellite Building.
The first phase, field testing from October 8 to 17, will see the update installed and tested under actual operating conditions.
The results will then undergo an independent safety assessment.
Subject to the assessments, the update will be permanently rolled out from November 28 to December 1.
KLIA said a full bussing service would run throughout the works as part of its operational contingency arrangements.
Passengers are advised to follow the signage to the bus lounge, where transfer buses will be available, or approach ground staff for assistance.
“Our priority is to ensure that the Aerotrain continues to provide a reliable and smooth service for passengers at KLIA,” KLIA chief operating officer Adam Nicholas Wilson said in a press statement today.
KLIA said the update follows the Aerotrain’s completion of 20,000 continuous operational hours.
It said the system has maintained 99.9 per cent availability since the Comprehensive Action Plan was completed in June.
Over the past 1.5 years, the Aerotrain has completed 167,481 return trips and carried about 23.55 million passengers, it added.

Title: Jealousy suspected in Polisas student murder; teen boyfriend remanded in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 7 — Police have recorded statements from three individuals to assist investigations into the death of a female student, who is believed to have been killed by her boyfriend at a house on Jalan Air Putih here yesterday.
Kuantan District Police Chief ACP Ashari Abu Samah said police had summoned the victim’s housemates to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
“The victim and the suspect had known each other for about a year, and the incident is believed to have stemmed from jealousy. Investigations are still ongoing,” he said when contacted today.
Earlier, police received an emergency call from the victim’s boyfriend at 4.32 am, following which the 19-year-old Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Polytechnic (POLISAS) student was found lying on a bed in a rented room on the ground floor of the house.
Police subsequently arrested a 19-year-old man at the scene, who has been remanded until next Monday to facilitate further investigations. — Bernama
